newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-PHILIPPOUSSIS AND RENEBERG REACH ARIZONA FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-PHILIPPOUSSIS AND RENEBERG REACH ARIZONA FINAL.

text.p: Big-hitting Australian Mark Philippoussis served his way into the final of the Arizona Tennis Classic Saturday where he will face eighth-seeded American Richey Reneberg.
Philippoussis rocketed 19 aces past American Chris Woodruff en route to a 4-6 7-6 6-2 victory in Saturday's first semifinal.
"It was a good battle," Woodruff said. "Playing him takes a toll on you, hammering the ball and hammering the ball. You can only hold on so long."
Reneberg used a solid ground attack to dismiss unseeded Swede Jonas Bjorkman 6-3 6-3.
Reneberg will be vying for the fourth title of his 10-year career against the huge-serving Australian.
"I've been playing well all week. I hope I have a little bit left for the final," said Reneberg, who scattered 12 unforced errors -- 20 fewer than his opponent -- in the 67-minute sweep.
The eighth seed took the first set as Bjorkman double-faulted at break point in the eighth game, leaving the 29th-ranked Reneberg to serve out the set.
In the second set, Reneberg led 5-3 and broke the Swede for the fourth time on his third match point when Bjorkman sprayed a backhand wide.

Philippoussis played an uneven match but managed to produce 45 winners compared with just 15 for Woodruff. The Australian also commited 38 unforced errors in the two hour and 10 minute match but just four in the third set.
"I didn't feel really 100 percent out there and still ended up coming through," said the 42nd ranked Philippoussis.
"That was very important when you're not at your best, physically or game-wise, and still come through to win."
Woodruff needed only a service break in the third game to take first set.

The 20-year-old Philippoussis managed to force a third set despite squandering a 5-2 lead and five set points in the second. He took the tie-break 7-5 with the help of a pair of aces and a ferocious forehand winner at set point.
In the third set, Philippoussis jumped out to another 5-2 lead, belting forehand winners at break points in games five and seven.
This time he did not allow Woodruff back into the set, instead serving out the victory with a 131 miles per hour (211 kph) ace on match point.
